samples.summary: Table-cell hit-testing never produces 'forward' affinity, so Home/End inside a cell now act on the previous visual line
samples.evidence: getVisualLineRange's table-cell branch (text-editor.ts:4029) now honours `lineAffinity`, defaulting to `this.cursor.lineAffinity`. But every cell cursor-placement path hard-codes 'backward': single click `this.cursor.moveTo(cellPos)` (1584, no affinity arg → Cursor.moveTo default 'backward', cursor.ts:28), double/triple/shift-click (1552/1562/1573), and resolveHFCellOffset returns `lineAffinity: 'backward'` unconditionally (4509, 4515). resolveOffsetInCellAtXY (4630) does not even return an affinity field. Consequence: click at the START of a soft-wrapped visual line inside a table cell yields offset == the wrap boundary with affinity 'backward'; getVisualLineRange now resolves that to the PREVIOUS visual line, so Home moves the caret up to the previous line's start and End moves it back to the previous line's end — before this change both correctly acted on the clicked line. The body path is safe only because findPositionAtPixel's affinityForOffset (find-position-at-pixel.ts:116) returns 'forward' there; the cell path has no equivalent.

samples.summary: moveVertical still calls findVisualLine with the 'forward' default, now inconsistent with the affinity-aware helpers
samples.evidence: `const info = findVisualLine(lb, pos);` (4165) keeps the new 'forward' default while the pixel hit-test one line above (4104 getPixelForPosition(pos, this.cursor.lineAffinity)) resolves the caret with 'backward'. At a character-wrap boundary with 'backward' affinity (reachable in one keystroke: End, or ArrowLeft from boundary+1) the caret is drawn at the end of line i, but findVisualLine reports lineIndex i+1, so `isFirstLine` is false and the 'Up in the first block → jump to lineStart' shortcut (4170) never fires; paginatedPixelToPosition clamps back to the same offset, leaving ArrowUp a no-op. Symmetrically `isLastLine` can fire one line early for ArrowDown, snapping to info.lineEnd. The task doc declares this a non-goal, but the change makes the two resolutions disagree where they previously agreed.

samples.summary: Cmd+Backspace can still delete every earlier visual line when affinity is 'forward' (e.g. immediately after Home)
samples.evidence: handleLineBackspace: when `lineStart.offset === pos.offset` it falls into `this.docDeleteText({blockId, offset: 0}, pos.offset)` (2853), deleting the whole block prefix rather than one visual line. handleHome sets affinity to 'forward' unconditionally (`this.cursor.moveTo(newPos, 'forward')`, 2793), so at the start of visual line i>0 getVisualLineStart returns that same offset and the destructive branch is still reachable in two keystrokes (Home, then Cmd+Backspace) — the exact data-loss the change's task doc claims to fix, only shifted from the 'backward' boundary case to the 'forward' line-start case.

samples.summary: getWrapAffinity uses the body layout and cannot see cell blocks, so post-typing affinity is 'backward' in headers/footers/table cells — which now changes Home/End
samples.evidence: getWrapAffinity (4083-4098) looks the block up in `this.getLayout()` (body layout) rather than `getActiveLayout()`, and table-cell blocks are not in `layout.blocks` at all, so it returns 'backward' for every caret position in a header, footer, or table cell. Callers at 322/548/576/636/687/733/3596/3651/3723/5178 set the cursor with that value. Previously that stale 'backward' only affected caret painting; with this change, typing text in a cell/header that wraps mid-token leaves the caret at the wrap boundary with 'backward' affinity, so a following Home/End now acts on the PREVIOUS visual line.

samples.summary: End can now move the caret backwards at a wrap boundary with trailing spaces
samples.evidence: getVisualLineEnd trims trailing spaces for non-last lines (4068-4073). With the new 'backward' resolution, a cursor already sitting exactly on the boundary (offset == lineEnd, e.g. after ArrowLeft from boundary+1) resolves to line i, and End returns lineEnd minus trailing spaces — i.e. pressing End moves the caret LEFT from where it already was. Previously the same keystroke resolved forward and moved the caret onto the next line. Small, arguably desirable, but it is a new non-monotonic End.

verdict.reason: All claimed facts check out in the repository. getVisualLineRange's cell branch honours lineAffinity with `ownsLineEnd = li === endLine - 1 || lineAffinity === 'backward'` (text-editor.ts:4029), so a wrap-boundary offset with 'backward' affinity resolves to the PREVIOUS visual line. Every table-cell caret placement path supplies 'backward': single click `this.cursor.moveTo(cellPos)` with no affinity arg (1584) and Cursor.moveTo's default is 'backward' (cursor.ts:28, field default line 13); double/triple/shift-click likewise (1552/1562/1573); resolveOffsetInCell/resolveOffsetInCellAtXY return only {blockId, offset} with no affinity (4619/4635/4808); resolveHFCellOffset hard-codes 'backward' (4509, 4515). A click at the left edge of a soft-wrapped cell line does yield exactly the wrap-boundary offset (offset accumulated over preceding lines at 4745-4751, then `offset + i` with i=0 at 4804-4808). Home/End then read that affinity by default (handleHome 2786, handleEnd 2799 -> getVisualLineStart/End defaults at 4053/4061), so they act on the previous visual line. The body path really does differ: find-position-at-pixel.ts:131/165 use affinityForOffset and can return 'forward'; no cell equivalent exists. The one nuance I found — cell caret rendering applies the same backward rule (peer-cursor.ts:196-205), drawing the caret at the previous line's end — does not refute the finding: it merely relocates the visible symptom (the click itself lands the caret on the previous visual line instead of the clicked one). Real logic bug in a core click/navigation flow; no guard elsewhere prevents it.
